messages:
emma-cs: Hey team — customer data-analytics-pro opened an escalation: their embeddings pipeline started failing yesterday with intermittent "Embedding dimension mismatch" errors and lots of tail latency. Happens for some requests and not others. They reported higher failure rate when traffic hits eu-west. I reproduced locally and saw two symptoms: 1) 400s with dimension mismatch, 2) requests routed to a US host with huge cold-start latencies. Sharing quick logs and repro below.

sahil: thanks emma. can you paste a minimal failing curl and the exact error payload? also which model name they are calling?

emma-cs: sample request we used:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"embedding-astro-1536","input":"foo"}'
```
Response (400):
```json
{"error":"Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but received 384","request_id":"req_01G..."}
```
We also tried forcing eu host: `https://eu.api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings` and that succeeded (1536-d vectors). The failure happens when requests hit the global api host and get routed to a different region.

ryan-mlops: interesting. that error is exactly what you'd get if the serving node is running a different model binary (or a different model variant) that emits 384-d vectors. possible causes: model catalog out-of-sync between regions, or smart-routing spilled traffic to a cheaper/smaller model variant during congestion. do we have autoscale/spillover events in eu-west yesterday?

infra-bot: [deploy-monitor] autoscale event: eu-west-1 GPU pool reached 95% at 2026-02-13T09:12:03Z. Spillover policy `embeddings:spill->fallback-region` triggered, routing 18% of traffic to nearest region (us-east-1).

alice-eng: that lines up. our fallback routing currently picks the nearest region and the nearest compatible model by name, but a compat check only compares model family, not embedding dim. so if us-east registered a variant `embedding-astro-compact-384` we incorrectly route to it.

sahil: ok, steps to repro for eng: 1) call global host without region header 2) set model to `embedding-astro-1536` 3) if routing goes to us-east-1 variant you'll get 384-d mismatch. simple curl to demonstrate: 
```bash
for i in {1..5}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n    -d '{"model":"embedding-astro-1536","input":"test $i"}' || true; \
  echo; \
done
```
If you hit the wrong region, response contains the JSON error above.

maya-support: customer asked for an immediate workaround they can apply from their side while we fix routing. They can explicitly hit the eu host, right?

alice-eng: yes — temporary mitigation: direct-region host or `X-Region` header. Examples:
- Use `https://eu.api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings`
- Or add header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` in the request
Both force region affinity and avoid spillover. Note: if the eu pool is fully saturated they may see increased latency or throttling rather than the mismatch error.

ryan-mlops: permanent fix options: 1) enforce embedding_dim check during routing so we only route to nodes whose model metadata embedding_dim matches requested model; 2) sync model catalog/variants across regions (prefer exact model names); 3) add a compatibility gate for fallback model variants to avoid smaller-dim fallbacks.

sahil: I dug into the logs to confirm the hypothesis. grep from node logs when error occurred: 
```
[2026-02-13T09:14:07Z] req=req_01G.. routed_region=us-east-1 routed_model=embedding-astro-compact-384 model_expected_dim=1536 model_emitted_dim=384
[2026-02-13T09:14:08Z] WARN: model_compatibility_check failed, but routing policy allowed fallback=true
```
So routing allowed fallback even though emitted dim didn't match.

emma-cs: customer also sent timing traces. When routed to us-east we saw p95>12s (cold-starts) vs eu p95 ~140ms. They were surprised because they expect global host to keep latency under 1s.

infra-bot: cold-start events: us-east-1 GPU nodes warmed from 0 to 3 at 2026-02-13T09:13:50Z (scale up). Estimated warm-up time for model `embedding-astro-compact-384` is ~9-11s which matches the observed tails.

alice-eng: immediate engineering mitigation I'll push now: 1) block fallback to models with differing embedding_dim in routing logic (hotfix), 2) add an alert when fallback policy routes to a model with embedding_dim != requested_dim. I'll open PR and run canary. ETA ~2hrs.

ryan-mlops: I'll coordinate capacity — we need to scale eu-west reserved pool and consider temporary credit of burst capacity for this customer if they want no risk of spillover. Maya, can you confirm if they're on Dedicated or Hosted?

maya-support: hosted. they are on a high-volume plan but not Dedicated. Customer asked about a guaranteed region pin (they're sensitive to data residency). They'd prefer region-only routing.

sahil: adding to runbook: how to validate model dims before routing:
1) call metadata: `GET /v1/models/embedding-astro-1536/metadata` -> returns `{"embedding_dim":1536, "version":"v3.2"}`
2) if metadata missing, treat as incompatible and do not fallback.

alice-eng: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pull/512 — implementing strict embedding_dim compatibility and an opt-in override for region affinity header. Canary started on routing cluster A. Will follow up when merged.

emma-cs: shared the temporary workaround with customer (hosted eu endpoint + X-Redwood-Region). They accepted and will switch their pipeline for the next 24h. They also asked for a postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix.

ryan-mlops: Proposed postmortem notes: root cause = fallback routing allowed model-family fallback without validating embedding dimension; contributing factors = eu-west capacity spike + catalog mismatch where us-east had a compact variant registered. Impact = dimension-mismatch errors for ~18% of traffic during spillover window and p95 latency spikes to 10-12s.

alice-eng: action items (assigned):
- alice-eng: push routing compatibility hotfix + monitor (in progress)
- ryan-mlops: request temporary burst capacity to eu-west pool; implement permanent capacity plan (in flight)
- sahil: update docs/runbook with model metadata check and example curl (PR queued)
- maya-support: confirm customer accepted workaround and record SLO impact in ticket

maya-support: confirmed workaround applied. customer will run for 24h and report if any further issues. They requested a follow-up once hotfix is live.

sahil: follow-up checks to run after hotfix: send 500 mixed-region requests to global host and assert no dimension mismatch errors, validate alerts for fallback events, and check p95 stays below 1.2s for eu-hosted calls.

emma-cs: thanks all. please post updates here when PR merges and when we have postmortem. Putting this on high priority for visibility. :exclamation: :eyes:

alice-eng: update: hotfix merged to canary at 1769005300, starting gradual rollout. will update when fully rolled out.

ryan-mlops: update: temporary eu-west burst granted for 24h to reduce spillover risk.

maya-support: customer notified and happy for now. will close the escalation once we confirm no regressions.

alice-eng: postmortem skeleton will be posted to /docs/postmortems/embedding-routing-dim-mismatch.md after we finalize.

emma-cs: closing notes: root cause, mitigation, customer workaround, and follow-ups recorded. leaving thread open until postmortem published.
